messages:
Asha: ran an apples-to-apples bench comparing two kernel selectors (selector-A vs selector-B) across synthetic Poisson load and our replay harness. Surprising tradeoffs: selector-B gives better steady throughput but significantly worse coldstart and autoscale behavior. TL;DR below.

Mike: drop the headline numbers? :eyes:

Asha: summary from replay harness (mixed-priority, 1k concurrent, avg prompt ~8s):
```
replay summary:
- steady p50: selector-B=7.9ms, selector-A=11.4ms
- steady p95: selector-B=58ms, selector-A=82ms
- coldstart p95 (first 45s): selector-B=520ms, selector-A=140ms
- time to attach one GPU (scale-up): selector-B=24s, selector-A=7s
- burst credits used/node during surge: selector-B=390, selector-A=120
```
Synthetic Poisson runs show similar steady-state gaps but smaller cold spikes on average.

Yuri: that's a large warmup gap. Do we know which subsystems are hot during the first minute? kernel init or KV behavior?

Asha: sampled flame and instrumented allocations. Top reasons:
```
0.48s  kernel_candidate_fingerprint()  # selector-B probes more shapes + tiny microbenchmarks
0.28s  kv_cache_prefetch()             # selector-B enqueues a larger prefetch set
0.18s  cuda_ctx_create()               # visible in first few attach ops
```
Selector-B spends extra CPU on per-model/shape heuristics which reduces tokens/ms later but pays a heavy first-touch tax.

Eva: could we cache the fingerprint result per model+sequence-bucket or make fingerprinting async so it doesn't block the first requests?

Asha: tried an async path: fingerprint scheduled off the hot path, with a lightweight fallback selector. Preliminary numbers: cold p95 improved from 520ms -> 190ms, steady p50/p95 unchanged. Tradeoffs: added complexity and occasional mis-choice on rare seq-lens.

benchbot: run complete: bench-replay-1995007777 uploaded to /bench/results/bench-replay-1995007777.json

Mike: paste the autoscale timeline and credit burn — curious how warmup correlates with credit usage.

Asha: timeline for a 2-minute surge starting at t=0 (nodes begin with 150 credits each):
```
00:00 surge start -> queue climbs fast
00:04 scale request triggered (policy)
00:09 new node allocated, initialization starts -> lots of KV misses
00:23 throughput ramps to target
00:30 credits remaining: selector-B=95, selector-A=210
01:00 credits remaining: selector-B=5, selector-A=85
```
Selector-B burned credits quickly during warmup due to aggressive prefetch + kernel microbench heat.

Yuri: that suggests Shared pools without prewarm will suffer. For Dedicated pools customers can prewarm nodes, so selector-B might be fine. Any regression vs baseline from last week's runs?

Asha: compared to last week's baseline (no fingerprinting):
- selector-B improves steady p50 by ~9% vs baseline
- but multiplies cold p95 by ~3.5x and increases credit burn ~3x
So net: wins for stable, low-churn traffic; loses for bursty traffic unless mitigated.

Eva: mitigation ideas: KV prefill on node attach, conservative kernel fallback for first N requests, or async fingerprint + correctness check. Also expose a toggle in Optimize/Console.

Asha: experimented with a conservative-first policy: on node add, mark kernel=fast-warmup for first 40 requests then flip. Results: cold p95 reduced ~50%, credit usage down ~35%, steady-state latency regressed slightly (~+3.8%).

Mike: what's the recommendation for rollout between Dedicated and Shared pools?

Asha: proposal:
- Dedicated pools: enable selector-B by default (customers get guidance to prewarm and set warmup windows).
- Shared pools: keep selector-A as default, enable selector-B behind an "aggressive-kernel" toggle plus these mitigations: conservative-first fallback, async fingerprinting, KV-prefill on scale events.
- Add a Console blurb for AEs about workload patterns that benefit from selector-B.

benchbot: ticket INF-3321 created: "kernel-selector warmup & autoscale mitigations" (owner=Asha)

Yuri: action items:
- [Asha] add a runnable harness script + flags to reproduce coldstart pattern and upload traces -> EOD
- [Mike] prototype async fingerprint + safety checks in CI harness -> next Wed
- [Eva] run cost estimate for KV prefill (traffic + latency tradeoffs) and propose prefill-size heuristics -> next Tue

Asha: harness command to reproduce (from infra bench node):
```
./bench/run_replay.sh --id=bench-replay-1995007777 --selector=selector-B --replay=replays/mixed1k.json --warmup=0s --record-trace
```
Use --warmup=30s or bump prefill threads to 4 to see much better cold p95. I also noticed setting prefill-threadpool=4 cut cold p95 another ~28%.

Mike: can you also draft a 2-paragraph Console note for sales about which customers should enable selector-B?

Asha: will draft and attach to the ticket. uploading flame graphs and the full result bundle to the bench artifact link now. :thumbsup:

Eva: great — this gives a clear path for defaults and short-term mitigations.

Asha: follow-up: will open a small spike to add async fingerprint tests in our CI harness and wire KV prefill flags into the runtime config. Ping me for raw traces if you want them.
